title: Karl Marx's birth chart
metaDescription: Karl Marx's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.3° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 16.3° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Taurus, but precisely: 14.3°, second decan, 10°–20°, under Mercury in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 3.9° Gemini, Venus was at 28.0° Taurus, Mars was at 21.0° Cancer. Read together: a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste for the substantial and the lasting; drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Neptune to Pluto, a square with 0.2° of slack. A square is the tradition’s engine room: two drives at cross purposes, and the friction is the horsepower. Behind it, the Sun trine Jupiter at 1.4°, and the Sun sextile Saturn at 1.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, five sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Moon in Taurus at 16.3° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Gemini at 3.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Venus in Taurus at 28.0° is in domicile; Mars in Cancer at 21.0° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Jupiter in Capricorn at 12.9° is in fall. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 earth, 3 water, 2 fire, 1 air by element and 5 mutable, 3 fixed, 2 cardinal by modality. Earth signs hold the scheme’s slow end, where results are measured in what survives rather than what starts. Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 11.9° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 16.3°.
